question: Are zero saved GEOVAR offsets (NOM 0) legal, what is the delta baseline for inconsistent saved geometry, and do inactive dimensions still resolve?

probes.z_nc.son: ANC NSCD NOM 0 with noncoincident REF1/REF2 - native SOLVED (errors log archived)
probes.z_w.son: SYM NSCD NOM 0, geometric span 1300, target 1300 - native SOLVED; bit-identical to literal litA (no move)
probes.z_w600.son: SYM NSCD NOM 0, geometric span 1300, target 600 - native SOLVED; bit-identical to literal l_delta (delta = target - geometric span, +-350 each side)
probes.z_scu.son: SYM SCUNI NOM 0 - native SOLVED at intake and through the sweep
probes.z_inact.son: all dimensions inactive (target == NOM) but ANC A2 geometrically inconsistent (NOM 0, offset 700) - native collapsed REF2 onto REF1; param output matches literal litC within 2.1e-6, not litK (6.9e-2)
probes.z_rad_errors.log: RAD NSCD NOM 0 intake and solve, 0 errors (probe file had a nonempty PS1 left from the SYM template; native accepts it - our parser keeps a loud adapter rejection there)

conclusions: NOM 0 is legal for every kind and header: ANC/SYM/RAD, NSCD and scaled alike.
The delta baseline is the geometric span between references, never the NOM field (bit-exact literal discrimination).

Dimensions resolve by real displacement regardless of NOM activity: an inconsistent inactive project still collapses/expands to its targets (A2 collapse verified at 2.1e-6 against a collapse literal).
A project is unchanged only when every dimension's application is a stored no-op; sub-cell deviations (~1e-9 relative) from file-write quantization and SI round-trips are phantoms.
Negative and zero targets intake and solve natively; degenerate resolved geometry still rejects loudly in our pipeline where Sonnet tolerates it.
